source_caption:
Connor Roy is easy to treat like comic relief in Succession, but that’s what makes him quietly tragic. As the oldest son, he was emotionally abandoned long before the main power struggle begins, and his absurd presidential campaign feels less like pure vanity than a desperate attempt to be seen by a family that never really took him seriously.

Succession (2018–2023), created by Jesse Armstrong, starring Brian Cox, Jeremy Strong, Kieran Culkin. A sharp and addictive drama about a powerful media family fighting for control, blending corporate warfare, emotional damage, and brutal dark comedy into one of television’s defining modern tragedies.

source_details.synopsis: Succession is an American satirical comedy-drama television series created by English screenwriter Jesse Armstrong that aired for four seasons on HBO from June 3, 2018, to May 28, 2023. The series centers on the Roy family, the owners of global media and entertainment conglomerate Waystar RoyCo, and their fight for control of the company amidst uncertainty about the health of the family's patriarch. Brian Cox portrays the family patriarch Logan Roy. His children are played by Alan Ruck as Connor, Jeremy Strong as Kendall, Kieran Culkin as Roman, and Sarah Snook as Shiv.
